# MCP tools reference

Every agent session reaches the daemon through `infantry mcp serve`, a stdio MCP server built into the `infantry`
binary. It asks the daemon for the tool list (`plugin_tools`), forwards each call (`plugin_tool_call` /
`plugin_tool_result`) and sends `notifications/tools/list_changed` when a plugin adds or removes a tool. The one tool it
answers itself is `infantry_watch_file`.

`infantry mcp serve` takes the connection flags (`--url`, `--endpoint`, `--endpoints`, `--token-file`, `--project`) and
the depth guardrails (`--mcp-depth`, `--max-depth`, `--max-spawns`, `--allow-kill-any`). It reads the session identity
from the environment the harness inherits (`INFANTRY_URL`, `INFANTRY_SESSION_ID`, `INFANTRY_PROJECT_ID`, `INFANTRY_ROLE`,
the token; the old `AGENTHQ_*` names are read as fallbacks) and `.infantry/mcp.json` in the working folder. Results longer
than the setting `limits.mcp.maxResultChars` are cut; a tool takes `detail` and `maxChars` to ask for more.

## Core tools (26)

From `rust/crates/infantry-daemon/src/compose/agent_tools.json`.

### `infantry_list_sessions` (read-only)

List the SESSIONS (running or past agent runs, not saved profiles) the Infantry AI daemon knows: id, agentId, role, provider, model, projectId, status.

- `limit` (integer): At most this many sessions (live ones first, then the most recent). Default: setting limits.tools.listLimit.
- `projectId` (string): Only this project's sessions. Omitted: a session caller's own project (everyone else: all). "all" lists every project (pm / owner callers only).

### `infantry_get_session` (read-only)

One session's status and the last lines of its transcript (from the daemon's replay buffer, bounded).

- `brief` (boolean): Omit the transcript: return only state, live state, last action and last output/event times.
- `lines` (integer): How many trailing transcript lines to return (default: setting limits.tools.sessionTailLines, 5).
- `sessionId` (string, required): Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

### `infantry_spawn`

Spawn an Infantry AI session for a role and/or an agent profile, optionally sending it a first task, OUTSIDE the board: it runs in the project folder and leaves every ticket untouched. Never use it for ticket work: start ticket work with infantry_ticket_start (or pass ticketId here, which does the same).

- `agentId` (string): Agent profile id; with role, it must be that profile's role.
- `effort` (string): Reasoning effort for the session: low, medium, high, xhigh or max (off = the harness default).
- `model` (string): Model id of that harness (infantry_list_harnesses lists them).
- `projectId` (string): Project the session belongs to (default: the caller's project).
- `provider` (string): Harness (provider id) the session runs: see infantry_list_harnesses. Omitted = the daemon's default.
- `role` (string): Role to spawn (role-first, like the `new` frame).
- `task` (string): Optional first prompt for the new session.
- `ticketId` (string): Start this board ticket instead (full id or its 8-char suffix), exactly as infantry_ticket_start.

### `infantry_prompt`

Send a prompt to an existing session (id or unique prefix). Slash commands are refused.

- `prompt` (string, required): The words to send to the agent.
- `sessionId` (string, required): Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

### `infantry_kill`

Kill a session (id or unique prefix). A pm (or the owner) may kill any session in its own project; other roles only sessions they spawned.

- `force` (boolean): Kill the process tree at once instead of after the grace period.
- `sessionId` (string, required): Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

### `infantry_list_harnesses` (read-only)

List the harnesses a ticket can run on: each harness id (the value of a ticket's provider) with its models (the values of its model), which one is the default, and whether its CLI is available. Pin them with infantry_ticket_create / infantry_ticket_update, then start the ticket with infantry_ticket_start.

### `infantry_usage` (read-only)

Read plan usage per meter: percent of the plan window used (the highest window), when it resets, points ahead/under an even burn, and how many ticket workers the pacing rule allows versus how many run. Text summary; pass json=true to append the full JSON report.

- `json` (boolean): Append the full JSON report after the text summary (default false).

### `infantry_usage_override`

Override the usage pacing allowance for a meter (owner and pm roles; setting usage.overrideRoles). value = a ticket-worker count, 'none' (no limit) or 'clear' (the pacing rule decides again). The override lasts hours hours, default until the meter resets (else 2h).

- `hours` (number): How long the override lasts, in hours (default: until the meter resets)
- `meter` (string, required): The meter to override (claude, codex, opencode-go, ...)
- `value` (string, required): A worker count, 'none' or 'clear'

### `infantry_pace` (read-only)

Read the pacing history the daemon recorded from the plan meters: per provider window the percent used, the pace delta, the projected landing at reset, the momentum and the forecast to reset.

- `provider` (string): Only this meter (claude, codex, opencode-go, ...)
- `samples` (string): "true" adds the newest raw samples per series; default off
- `sinceHours` (number): Only points from the last N hours (default: all)
- `window` (string): Only this window label (e.g. '5h limit')

### `infantry_message`

Send a message (COMMS mail) to another agent by session id, agent id or role, or to the owner. Replies go in the same thread with replyTo. Returns the message id.

- `allowCrossProject` (boolean): Allow a recipient in another project.
- `body` (string, required): The message text.
- `key` (string): Optional dedupe key for kind (a build run id, a ticket id): the same kind+key wakes a recipient at most once, across mails and ticket comments.
- `kind` (string): Optional notice kind (e.g. build.success, build.failed, ticket.done.ping). With a kind, the setting notify.wake.kinds decides: a kind that wakes is mailed, any other lands in the recipient's attention inbox with no mail and no turn.
- `needsInput` (boolean): The recipient must answer.
- `replyTo` (string): Message id (or 8-char prefix) this answers; keeps the thread.
- `subject` (string): Optional subject line.
- `to` (string, required): Recipient: session id, agent profile id, role id, or owner.

### `infantry_inbox` (read-only)

List the messages addressed to you (id, from, subject, state). unreadOnly limits it to the ones you have not read.

- `limit` (integer): At most this many, newest first.
- `unreadOnly` (boolean): Only unread messages.

### `infantry_read`

Read one message in full by id (8-char prefix works) and mark it read.

- `id` (string, required): The message id from infantry_inbox.

### `infantry_session_remove`

Remove a session from the list. A live session is refused unless force=true, which ends it first. Only the pm or the owner (own project), or the session's spawner, may remove one. An id no session matches is already gone: OK with outcome already-removed.

- `force` (boolean): End a live session and remove it in one step.
- `sessionId` (string, required): Session id or unique prefix.

### `infantry_agent_list` (read-only)

Every agent the daemon's agent registry holds (built-in roles and plugin-contributed agents): id, name, whether it is enabled, who contributed it.

### `infantry_agent_get` (read-only)

One agent of the registry in full: its definition (instructions or role, default harness/model/context limit, tools, schedule, ui hints), contributor and enabled state.

- `id` (string, required): the agent id (see infantry_agent_list)

### `infantry_agent_enable`

Re-enable a disabled agent (non-agent caller only).

- `id` (string, required): the agent id (see infantry_agent_list)

### `infantry_agent_disable`

Disable an agent: new sessions of it are refused, running ones carry on (non-agent caller only).

- `id` (string, required): the agent id (see infantry_agent_list)

### `infantry_waiting`

Flag YOUR session 'active but waiting' (on) or not waiting (off). Use it when your turn is about to end while you wait on a process (a build, a long test, a background job): your card shows 'waiting' with your reason instead of looking idle, and no watcher nudges you. It turns itself off when your next turn starts, and expires after untilMinutes (+ a grace). get = read the flag. The CLI does the same without MCP: infantry waiting on --reason "..." [--minutes N] | off.

- `mode` (string, required): 
- `reason` (string): mode on: what you are waiting for (required).
- `untilMinutes` (integer): mode on: how long you expect to wait (omit = the default setting).

### `infantry_pod_state` (read-only)

Summary of the pod: saved PROFILES (templates, not running) grouped by role under `agents`, SESSIONS by status; optionally one project's `roster` (its live AGENTS, BUSY/IDLE/OFFLINE: who can be assigned work) and one pod's node state.

- `podId` (string): Include this pod's state and nodes.
- `projectId` (string): Include this project's live roster (running agents, not profiles). Default: the caller's own project; "all" (pm / owner callers only) covers every project.

### `infantry_session_restart`

Restart a session: the same session, a fresh conversation (its next turn is a first turn). A running turn is refused unless force=true, which stops it first.

- `force` (boolean): Stop a running turn first.
- `sessionId` (string, required): Session id, or a unique prefix of one.

### `infantry_capability_list` (read-only)

List the capabilities the loaded plugins offer (id, module, runs, action, available). Call one by its dotted id from a script: ih.call("id", {...}).

### `infantry_attention_raise`

Raise an item on the owner's attention list (kind, outcome, detail; optional ticketId / sessionId). For scripts and agents that report something the owner must see.

- `detail` (string, required): What the owner reads, at most 2000 characters.
- `kind` (string, required): An attention kind, e.g. session_resumed, stalled, unreported.
- `outcome` (string, required): A short machine word for what happened, e.g. resumed_after_restart.
- `sessionId` (string): 
- `ticketId` (string): 

### `infantry_prompt_answer`

Answer a question (or tool approval) an agent is BLOCKED on: the answer returns to its blocked tool call. When questions.route sends a session's questions to you (the pm), the wake line names the promptId. promptId + answers (option labels; several only for a multi-select question) and/or otherText; for a tool approval pass decision (allow_once, allow_session, allow_always, deny). escalate=true hands a pm-then-owner question to the owner instead. With no promptId it lists the open prompts. Only the owner or the pm; the CLI does the same: infantry prompt answer <promptId> --answer <label> [--text <t>] | --escalate.

- `answers` (array): Option labels.
- `decision` (string): Tool approvals only: allow_once, allow_session, allow_always, deny.
- `escalate` (boolean): Hand a pm-then-owner question to the owner.
- `otherText` (string): Your own words (when the question allows it).
- `promptId` (string): 

### `infantry_ask`

Ask the owner ONE decision: the question in plain words, 2 to 8 answer options (2 to 4 reads best), the recommended option and a one-line reason. It shows as a decision mail at the top of the owner's Mail inbox (desktop and phone) with one button per option and a free-text answer. Non-blocking: carry on; the owner's answer arrives in your session as mail on thread question:<id>. Rate-limited per agent (3 open, 6 an hour).

- `defaultAfterMin` (integer): Optional: auto-pick the recommended option after this many minutes (1-1440) if the owner has not answered.
- `options` (array, required): 2 to 8 answers: plain labels, or {label, description}.
- `question` (string, required): The decision, in plain words (max 2000 characters).
- `reason` (string, required): Why you recommend it, one line (max 200 characters).
- `recommended` (string, required): The label of the option you recommend.

## Plugin tools

Declared in each official plugin's `module.json` (`daemon.tools`). The plugin answers the call; its arguments
are described in the tool's description. `kind` is what the call does (`read` or `write`), `action` the permission it needs.

### Infantry_Cards

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cards_list` | read | `cards.read` | The chat card types installed plugins declare: type, module, summary (capability cards.list). |
| `cards_show` | read | `cards.show` | The spec an agent needs to write one card type (capability cards.show): args type. |

### Infantry_Chat

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `infantry_announce` | write | `mail.send` | Announce one message to every live agent of your project (one COMMS mail each). Only the roles in setting announce.allowedRoles (default owner, pm) may announce. |
| `infantry_inbox` | read | `mail.read` | Your COMMS inbox: counts and one line per item, newest unread first. Params: limit, offset, unreadOnly, previews. |
| `infantry_read` | read | `mail.read` | Read one message of your inbox in full and mark it read. |
| `infantry_message` | write | `mail.send` | Send COMMS mail to an agent id, a role, a session id, or role@project (needs allowCrossProject). |
| `infantry_projects` | read | `mail.read` | Look up projects: id, name, description and the roles with a live session. |

### Infantry_Docs

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `docs_list` | read | `docs.read` | The bundled docs pages: name and one-line title (capability docs.list). |
| `docs_show` | read | `docs.show` | One docs page text by name (capability docs.show): args page. |

### Infantry_Mcp

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `infantry_mcp` | read | `mcp.read` | MCP servers. op list: every server. op status: one server (name). op my_tools: the servers THIS session was handed and why. op grants: who was granted what. add/remove/enable/disable/grant/revoke are refused to agents (ask the PM or owner). |

### Infantry_Notes

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `infantry_memory` | read | `memory.read` | Read and write knowledge notes (what `infantry memory show\|search\|index\|save\|delete` does). action=show needs name; action=search needs query (matches names, descriptions and bodies); action=index lists notes; action=write needs name, description, body (replaces the note; optional folder); action=update needs name and content (appends; with find it replaces that one exact passage); action=delete needs name. scope: project (default), global (shared by every project on this install; writing needs a role in setting knowledge.globalWriteRoles, default pm), role (your role's notes), session; show without scope tries role, then project (which includes global), then session. |

### Infantry_Plugins

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `infantry_plugin_list` | read | `plugins.read` | Every plugin on this host: version, class, tier, enabled, grants, licence, update offer. |
| `infantry_plugin_search` | read | `plugins.read` | Search the plugin catalogs by text (id, description or tag) and optional tag. |
| `infantry_plugin_show` | read | `plugins.read` | Check a plugin reference and show its class, signer, licence and requested grants. Installs nothing. |
| `infantry_plugin_status` | read | `plugins.read` | One installed plugin state (version, enabled, grants, update offer). |
| `infantry_plugin_list_import` | write | `plugins.request` | Import a plugin list (file path or URL) as a community catalog source. Installs nothing. |
| `infantry_plugin_request` | write | `plugins.request` | Ask the owner to install a plugin with exactly the grants it requests. Nothing is installed until the owner answers yes. |
| `plugins_status` | read | `plugins.status` | One plugin state, or installed:false (capability plugins.status). |

### Infantry_Settings

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `infantry_project_config_get` | write | `projects.save` | Read a project per-role caps on concurrent agents (a role not listed runs 1) and its task routing rules. |
| `infantry_project_config_set` | write | `projects.save` | Set a project per-role caps, autoRemoveDoneWorkers, routingRules (replace), experiment switches or generic project data. |
| `infantry_project_delete` | destructive | `projects.delete` | Delete a project and its workspaces. Refused while a session of the project is live unless force is true. Tickets and sessions are not touched. |
| `infantry_settings_get` | read | `settings.read` | Read a setting effective value and the scope it comes from (session > role > project > app > default). |
| `infantry_settings_set` | write | `settings.save` | Set a setting at a scope (app, project, role or session) with the target ids. |

| `infantry_sites_ssh_exec` | write | `sites.servers.ssh` | Run a shell command on one of your hosting servers over SSH (args: server?, command, timeoutSec?). |
| `infantry_sites_ssh_upload` | write | `sites.servers.ssh` | Write a small text file on one of your hosting servers over SSH (args: server?, path, content). |

### Infantry_Triggers

| Tool | Kind | Action | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `triggers_list` | read | `triggers.read` | List the triggers: {kind?, projectId?} -> an array of triggers (capability triggers.list). |
| `triggers_save` | write | `triggers.save` | Create (no id) or edit a trigger (capability triggers.save); answers the saved trigger. |
| `triggers_delete` | destructive | `triggers.delete` | Delete a trigger and its event log: {id} (capability triggers.delete). |
| `triggers_fire` | write | `triggers.fire` | Feed one manual event to a trigger now: {id} (capability triggers.fire); answers the trigger after it. |
